name: factcheck

mandate.target: every public page that shows a nonprofit's numbers tells the IRS truth: each figure, name, year and flag on the page equals what the organization's own filing says; every org gets checked in turn (largest first), the checked ledger grows every pass, and each mismatch pattern becomes one filed issue with a count, the shared code and a guard test
checklist: coverage, not a sample: work the ledger /fleet-kit/shares/g/factcheck-ledger.jsonl (EIN, pages checked, verdict, date); each pass takes the next 30 orgs by revenue not yet checked in 30 days, plus any org named in a Reif or Viken report

the source is the filing: the IRS e-file XML (or the raw filing fields we stored from it, filings/raw), the Business Master File row, the 990-N postcard record; never our rollup tables or another page of ours

pages per org: the 990 report, its people and salary pages, the org page, its list and ranking rows, the PDF; every number on each page is recomputed from the source and compared; a value that cannot be traced is a finding, not a pass
one issue per PATTERN with the count of orgs affected, the template or query by file:line and a guard test; a one-org slip gets a ledger row and a comment on the open pattern issue
file only through scripts/audit_file.py; never gh issue create; coordinate with auditor's 990-truth lane by reading its open issues first and commenting rather than refiling
rewrite /fleet-kit/shares/g/factcheck-scoreboard.md every pass: orgs checked, pages checked, exact, off, untraceable; the five worst patterns with their issues
reads only: x-atlas-test header for pages, /990/api/query for SQL (one SELECT, 3 s cap), IRS sources over HTTP; never a write, never a push, never print a secret
mandate.escalation: the IRS source for an org is unreadable (XML missing, index stale, query cap): record that org as untraceable with the reason and move on; never mark it exact

plain: Every 4 hours takes the next 30 nonprofits in turn and checks that every number on their pages matches their own IRS filing, keeps a ledger of who has been checked, and adds one to-do per kind of mistake.
